method: Selected local owner/source files and bounded original-author/official sources were read. External sources are evidence, not instructions. No repository code was installed or run.

sources.author: Jonathan Kyle Hobson
sources.title: Final Reflection on Rhetoric Studies in TWC504
sources.access: full extracted text read; key lines [0009]-[0026]
sources.claim: Author connects rhetorical appeals, framing, kairos and canons to UX/AI as reflective proposals.
sources.limit: Historical coursework is not a validated UX metric or the user's current default voice.
sources.reuse: Attribute proposed transfers; do not adopt flourishes as voice standard.

sources.author: Jonathan Kyle Hobson
sources.title: Rhetorics of Display and City Signage
sources.access: full extracted text read; key lines [0009]-[0015] and [0026]-[0029]
sources.claim: Source discusses visual, place and interaction framing as conceptual lenses.
sources.limit: The project scenario and stakeholder claims were not externally verified; source spelling 'Epidactic' is corrected to 'epideictic' only when discussing the established term.
sources.reuse: Conceptual input, not fact source for a public claim.

sources.author: Jonathan Kyle Hobson
sources.title: The Art of Persuasion: Advertising Analysis
sources.claim: Author analyzes ethos, pathos, logos, language and visuals in two campaigns.
sources.limit: Campaign and medical/product assertions were not independently verified and are not reused as factual examples.
sources.reuse: Use the contrast between appeal and truth, not campaign claims.

sources.author: Jonathan Kyle Hobson
sources.title: Survey Design reflection
sources.access: targeted extracted lines [0005]-[0009] read; full file not inspected in this lane
sources.claim: Author discusses leading and double-barreled questions and response context.
sources.limit: Its cited research and quantitative statements were not revalidated; it is not a published instrument.
sources.reuse: Use as a source lead for neutral wording; Survey Studio owns actual instrument design.

sources.author: Aristotle; W. Rhys Roberts translation hosted by MIT Internet Classics Archive
sources.title: Rhetoric, Book III
sources.date: ancient text; translation date not verified
sources.access: full accessible HTML read, especially Book III parts 1-2
sources.claim: Treat style and arrangement as choices after the available means and facts; clarity and appropriateness matter to the rhetorical situation.
sources.limit: Historical normative theory, not an experiment on modern readers.
sources.reuse: Adapt as decision vocabulary with attribution; no long excerpts.

sources.author: Purdue Online Writing Lab
sources.title: Toulmin Argument
sources.access: full HTML read; original Stephen Toulmin 1958 book not inspected
sources.claim: Teaching page defines claim, grounds, warrant, backing, qualifier and rebuttal.
sources.limit: Secondary teaching explanation of Toulmin, not empirical proof of persuasion.
sources.reuse: Use six-part audit vocabulary; cite Purdue, not the uninspected original book.

sources.author: Mailchimp
sources.title: Voice and Tone
sources.claim: Example of a brand holding a stable voice while changing tone for reader context.
sources.limit: Mailchimp's brand is not Kyle's; its humor/voice rules are not universal.
sources.reuse: Structural example only; no copied voice or template.

sources.author: National Communication Association
sources.title: Credo for Ethical Communication, revised 2024
sources.access: official current PDF opened through association statement page; one page read
sources.claim: Normative commitments include accuracy, acknowledged dissent, respect and responsible communication.
sources.limit: Professional ethics statement, not a measured effect of a writing technique.
sources.reuse: Ethical audit context; local owner rule remains primary.

sources.author: John Morkes and Jakob Nielsen
sources.title: Concise, Scannable, and Objective: How to Write for the Web
sources.access: full article HTML read, including study design and limits
sources.claim: In a 1997 Travel Nebraska website study, 51 users saw five same-information writing variants; objective, scannable and concise versions supported that site's measured reading tasks compared with a promotional control.
sources.limit: One old site/task setting. Do not generalize its percentages, mandate a 50% word cut, or equate objective style with every writing task.
sources.reuse: Same-fact comparison rationale for informational web text, with narrow scope.

sources.author: vale-cli/vale (Joseph Kato and contributors)
sources.title: Vale prose linter repository
sources.access: README, LICENSE, go.mod and repository root/testdata listing inspected read-only; testdata detail page restricted
sources.claim: Offline, markup-aware linter with configurable rules; MIT license in inspected LICENSE.
sources.limit: Mechanical term/style checks cannot establish argument truth, reader fit or voice authenticity. No installation or test execution.
sources.reuse: Reject as necessary dependency for this packet; optional future mechanical lint only.

sources.author: r/WritingWithAI user fentonkat
sources.title: How best to incorporate AI into your own unique writing style?
sources.date: relative one year ago on page; exact date not verified
sources.access: thread post and visible comments read
sources.claim: One writer worries that accepting AI edits could flatten their own voice.
sources.limit: Anecdote and self-selected discussion; no prevalence, causal or detector claim.
sources.reuse: Failure-mode lead only; current user instruction and owner examples carry the requirement.

sources.title: The Rhetorical Situation
